$why: Moved out of claude.sh on 2026-08-16. THE WRITER PROMPT -- the one the whole pipeline exists
to send, and the last and largest to leave the script.
Twenty-six of its sections were command substitutions, each carrying its own HEADING inside
the substitution: reviewer feedback, verification criteria, codeline facts, test criteria,
dependency contracts, cross-codeline contracts, the brownfield policy. The words the writer
reads were assembled by shell conditionals spread over sixty lines and could not be read as a
prompt anywhere. The caller composes each section and passes it.
VERIFIED BY RECONSTRUCTION rather than by execution. Several sections shell out to jq against
the real PRD, so running the original with sample values proves nothing. Substituting every
placeholder back and requiring byte equality with the heredoc proves what is actually at risk:
that nothing was dropped, reordered or reworded. What the substitutions evaluate to is
unchanged, because the caller passes the same expressions.
description: The implementation prompt sent to the story writer.
body:
